pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High inference tail latency observed for hosted region-us-west-2, 90th p90 > 1200ms (detected 03:12 UTC). Auto-alerting team.

sam_oncall: on it, jumping in now. any customer impact visible?

ashley_eng: seeing error spike and slow tails on the runtime metrics, kv_cache_miss_rate up ~8x, batching latency also up.

michael_sre: logging shows large number of partial KV cache evictions during busy windows, likely due to recent rollout of LRU tuning (rolled at 02:50 UTC).

lisa_prodops: flagged support — a handful of customers reported degraded chat latency. No data exfiltration.

sam_oncall: immediate mitigation: roll traffic to fallback model variant (less optimized) + increase replica count in dedicated pool. Can someone flip the rollout?

ashley_eng: I can revert the LRU tuning flag to previous value. Pushing config rollback now: `curl -XPOST https://cfg.local/revert -d '{"kv_lru_ratio":0.6}'`

deployer-bot: deploy started: cfg-revert-2026-06-03 by ashley_eng, build 0.19.2 -> deploying to us-west-2

sam_oncall: switching routing: using policy `regional-fallback` to send 30% traffic to variant B as hotfix (canary)

michael_sre: autoscaling increased dedicated pool from 8->12 GPUs. Should absorb backlog.

ashley_eng: config revert completed, kv_cache_miss_rate trending down. Batching queue lengths decreasing.

sam_oncall: good. keep an eye on p95/p99 for next 30m. Any idea root cause?

ashley_eng: early hypothesis: LRU tuning change increased churn across KV shards, combined with slight change in request prefix distribution, led to KV cache thrash. Also recent quantization rollout yesterday might have changed tokenization leading to different prefix patterns — need to verify.

michael_sre: agree. we'll need to correlate the LRU change, quantization flag deployment, and new batching heuristics.

lisa_prodops: customer impact: 8 customers saw >2x latency for 3-15 minutes. Not widespread but significant for a few PLG customers. Support already notified.

sam_oncall: post-incident plan: schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Action items below — assign owners.

ashley_eng: ACTION: reproduce with synthetic workload that mirrors prefix diversity; owner: ashley_eng; ETA: EOD tomorrow.

michael_sre: ACTION: add KV cache telemetry to include per-shard eviction trace and correlate with rollout markers; owner: michael_sre; ETA: 3 days.

lisa_prodops: ACTION: customer outreach draft + impact summary; owner: lisa_prodops; ETA: 6 hours.

sam_oncall: ACTION: add automated rollback runbook to include `cfg revert` and `regional-fallback` routing steps; owner: sam_oncall; ETA: 24 hours.

ashley_eng: quick note: quantization flag may be contributing; I'll spin a canary with old quantization + old LRU to test.

michael_sre: also schedule a controlled canary where we toggle batching heuristics back to previous settings; want to confirm whether batching latency interacts with cache churn.

sam_oncall: good. tracking doc: https://redwood-internal/incident-tracker/3668801234 (will put timeline and logs).

deployer-bot: deploy completed: cfg-revert-2026-06-03 to us-west-2 (success)

ashley_eng: monitoring shows p95 back to baseline, p99 mostly improved. I'll leave extra alerting sensitivity up for 12 hours.

lisa_prodops: support update sent to impacted customers, included mitigation steps and ETA for full postmortem.

sam_oncall: thanks all. Postmortem invite: `calendar: postmortem - KV cache thrash & rollout interaction` tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Please bring logs and timelines.

michael_sre: adding follow-up: we should have a small playbook for combined rollout of quantization + cache tuning in the future (staggered canaries).

ashley_eng: noted, will draft playbook after reproduce work.

sam_oncall: last check — any remaining blockers?

ashley_eng: none from infra side. Will follow up with detailed reproduction steps in tracker.

michael_sre: none. closing pager. :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: PAGING cleared by sam_oncall at 03:42 UTC.

sam_oncall: closing thread here, will update postmortem doc after meeting. Thanks everyone :pray:
